# Jānis Ruško (Janis Rusko)

Jānis Ruško, professionally also using the name Janis Rusko, is a senior expert in chemical risk assessment at BIOR in Riga. His work focuses on chemical risk assessment for food safety, integrated chemical evidence, dietary exposure assessment, risk-benefit assessment, risk prioritisation, evidence synthesis, guidance, and policy-facing decision support.

Analytical chemistry and non-target analysis are the technical foundation of the profile. The current research direction is evidence infrastructure for chemical risk assessment: structuring fragmented evidence, improving prioritisation, and developing practical decision-support methods.

## Current Emphasis

- Integrated evidence infrastructure combining monitoring and occurrence data, food-consumption information, toxicological reference values, scientific literature, and predictive toxicology evidence. AI-assisted literature extraction is one supporting method for expanding and structuring occurrence evidence.
- Transparent risk-ranking, uncertainty, and monitoring-prioritisation methods for identifying evidence gaps and directing assessment and monitoring resources.
- Applied exposure, chemical-risk, and risk-benefit assessments designed for interpretable conclusions, proportionate guidance, and policy-facing decisions.

## Selected Work

- From Data to Decisions: postdoctoral research project 1.1.1.9/LZP/1/24/124, 2025-ongoing, developing structured decision-support methods that combine occurrence and monitoring data, food consumption, toxicological reference values, scientific literature, predictive toxicology evidence, and uncertainty. Current progress includes completion of the first data-collection and harmonisation work package, continued toxicological-reference-value integration, initiation of consumption-data linkage, and further development of risk-prioritisation methods. Official project page: https://bior.lv/en/projekts/the-scientific-institute-bior-in-cooperation-with-the-latvian-council-of-science-lcs-is-implementing-the-research-application-no-1-1-1-9-lzp-1-24-124-from-data-to-decis/ Progress update: https://bior.lv/en/project-news/updates-on-project-no-1-1-1-9-lzp-1-24-124-for-the-period-from-2-january-2026-to-30-june-2026/
- Systematic review of persistent and emerging environmental contaminants in edible bee products: ongoing review of occurrence evidence supporting evidence synthesis, data reuse, and risk prioritisation. Source: https://bior.lv/en/project-news/updates-on-project-no-1-1-1-9-lzp-1-24-124-for-the-period-from-2-january-2026-to-30-june-2026/

## Selected Outputs

- 2026: Deterministic Pilot Risk-Benefit Assessment of Latvian Inland Fish: Safe Weekly Consumption Guidance. Foods. Risk-benefit guidance. https://doi.org/10.3390/foods15050901
- 2021: Phenolic Profiles of Raw Mono- and Polyfloral Honeys from Latvia. Journal of Food Composition and Analysis. Analytical foundation. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfca.2021.103813
- 2020: Non-target and Suspected-target Screening for Potentially Hazardous Chemicals in Food Contact Materials: Investigation of Paper Straws. Food Additives & Contaminants: Part A. Non-target screening. https://doi.org/10.1080/19440049.2020.1711969
- 2021: Rapid Determination of Pharmaceuticals in Wastewater by Direct Infusion HRMS Using Target and Suspect Screening Analysis. Science of the Total Environment. Screening methods. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.142688

## Credentials

- Senior expert in chemical risk assessment at BIOR.
- Alternate member of EFSA's Management Board, 2022-present.
- PhD in analytical chemistry, University of Latvia.
- COST Management Committee member for Latvia: Agrifood-OneAI (CA25159; starts September 2026) and BeSafeBeeHoney (CA22105).
